beats.say: This Indian well has 3,500 steps, and its own cool air.
It is Chand Baori, in Abhaneri, Rajasthan, built more than a thousand years ago.
Rajasthan is dry most of the year. Most of its rain falls in the four monsoon months.
In the monsoon, the giant pit fills up like a tank. Then, month after month, the water sinks lower.
With an ordinary well, your rope gets too short. Here, the steps simply follow the water down, thirteen levels deep.
The steps zig-zag in double flights down three of its walls.
At the bottom, deep stone walls block the sun, and the water cools the air as it evaporates, by several degrees.
A thousand years before air conditioning, people walked down a well to cool off.
